model_output.verdict: Your Army logistics and maintenance work comes through immediately, and the results back up your move toward operations supervision. I’d want to talk to you.
write_up: Your resume makes a strong case for the move from Army maintenance and logistics into operations supervision. You show both the people you led and the equipment and readiness you were responsible for!

The vehicle readiness line is a great model: it gives the starting and ending rates and names the two changes you made. Your progression from mechanic to platoon sergeant is easy to follow, and your target role is clear at the top.

Your resume is unlikely to be what holds you back. Competition for the roles you choose will matter too. For civilian applications, consider spelling out military terms where a recruiter outside defense might not know them, and add what you taught the junior mechanics.

cards.line: - Accountable for $14M of vehicles, tools, and equipment with zero losses on three annual inventories
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this. The equipment value and inventory record give a recruiter a concrete picture of what you were accountable for.
A recruiter can see how many mechanics you trained, but not what you taught them. Naming the training would show more of your technical work.

cards.line: - Led, trained, and evaluated 38 soldiers across maintenance, supply, and fuel sections

cards.question: What decision did you make about the direction or priorities of those sections?

cards.cannot_tell: For maintenance operations roles, move this above the leadership line. The before and after makes your improvement work memorable.

fit.note: Your maintenance and logistics leadership gives you a strong basis for civilian operations roles. When applying outside defense, make the connection between Army terms and the employer’s work easy to follow.
